clue.text: Figure curtailing the misery of Christmas?

parts.note: DEC is short for December, the month of Christmas

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, so the last letter comes off the phrase built from the misery of Christmas

parts.note: agony is great misery

explanation.surface: A grumble about how unhappy the festive season makes someone, posed as a question about a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the misery of Christmas' reads as December's agony, DEC AGONY; 'curtailing' takes off its final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Money which talks of grief

indicators.note: talks of signals that a word for grief is spoken, and its sound gives the letters

parts.note: dolour is a literary word for grief or sorrow

explanation.surface: Money is said to speak of sorrow, as if wealth brought only sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is the currency unit of the US and many other countries, so it is money.

clue.text: Author has books in head

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cape or headland is a head of land jutting into the sea
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A writer keeps reading matter in mind, carrying books in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: Truman Capote is the author, '2', whose works supply the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was an American author, of In Cold Blood among others.

clue.text: Dress up a day in advance for lover

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for dress is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rig out is to dress

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
FRI is short for Friday, a day of the week

explanation.surface: Someone dresses up a day early to see their sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A girlfriend is a female partner or lover.

clue.text: Perfect cake rises in ancient region of Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue, rises says the pieces read upwards, so the whole string is turned around

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or perfect, read here as the letters A and I
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A flawless cake goes up in the oven somewhere in old Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is read as the letters A and I; 'rises' turns the whole run upwards, as suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia was an ancient land along the Nile in what is now Sudan and southern Egypt.

clue.text: Old European region, half crushed by crusher

indicators.note: crushed by says one piece is squeezed inside the crusher

parts.note: a boa constrictor kills by crushing its prey
hemi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: An old region of Europe is half-destroyed by something that crushes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crusher' looks like a machine but is the constricting snake, which squeezes the half inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia was a historical kingdom in central Europe, now the west of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Fly out of control following alarm over zero pressure and 15

indicators.note: following places the shuffled fly after the alarm

parts.note: a bell sounds an alarm

indicators.note: out of control says the letters of fly are thrown into disorder

parts.note: O looks like zero
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: An insect zooms wildly after a bell rings, under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' refers to the answer at 15-down, CRASH-LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A belly flop is a dive landing flat on the stomach, a clumsy crash landing in the water.

clue.text: A greeting from the heavens?

definitions.meaning: a call of welcome, as in hello or salute
pellets of ice that fall from the sky

explanation.definitionFit: Hail means both a salute of welcome and frozen rain falling from the sky.

clue.text: If man's colour scheme changes, those adapting to it entertained by this work of 2?

definitions.text: those adapting to it entertained by this work of 2

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the phrase before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Creatures that adapt to someone's changing colours are amused by a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Chameleons adapt to a colour scheme by changing their own colour; '2' is CAPOTE, who wrote this book.
explanation.definitionFit: Music for Chameleons is a 1980 collection by Truman Capote, and chameleons are the creatures that adapt to colours.

clue.text: Girl tricked a reported killer of South America

indicators.note: reported says the words are spoken, and their sound gives the letters

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name; conned means tricked; the indefinite article, A

explanation.surface: A girl fooled a supposed murderer in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'Anna conned a' sounds like the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a huge constricting snake of South American rivers, a deadly predator.

clue.text: Knock over reject who's shunned

indicators.note: to knock something over tips it upside down, so the word is turned around

parts.note: to repel is to reject or drive away

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a person nobody wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper, figuratively, is an outcast avoided by everyone.

clue.text: Case collapses on what's hot and what's not

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: a balti is a spicy curry, something hot

indicators.note: collapses says the letters of case fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A packing case falls apart, perhaps in a magazine column on what is fashionable and what is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's hot and what's not' looks like a fashion list; here BALTI is the hot dish and the definition is 'what's not', i.e. not hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic Sea is a cold northern sea, so it is something that is not hot.

clue.text: See 25
Mirror essential to the choreography

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Mirrors are vital to dance choreography, as in a rehearsal studio.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to mirror, repeating or reflecting something back.

clue.text: Holyrood debtor once fiddling with Lady Barbie

indicators.note: fiddling with something messes it about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish debtor tinkers with a lady's Barbie doll.
explanation.walkthrough: Holyrood Abbey in Edinburgh was a sanctuary where debtors could escape arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey laird was a debtor who took refuge in the sanctuary of Holyrood Abbey, Edinburgh.

clue.text: Work of 2 incorporated ancestors?

parts.note: Inc is the abbreviation for incorporated, used after US company names
old blood suggests one's ancestral line, forebears

explanation.surface: A Capote book seems to describe a company of forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cold Blood is Truman Capote's 1966 non-fiction novel.

clue.text: Precipitate found in small amount of liquid and ditch

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: cl is a centilitre, a small measure of liquid
precipitate as an adjective means rash or hasty

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: a precipitate appears in a little liquid, which is then thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precipitate' and 'liquid' suggest a chemistry lab; precipitate means RASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch an aircraft is to bring it down in an emergency, to crash-land it.

clue.text: Berth farthest from birth?

parts.note: a bed, or berth, at the opposite end of life from the cradle: the one where life ends

explanation.definitionFit: A deathbed is the bed one dies in, as far from birth as a life goes.

clue.text: Ecstasy, the true sublime

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: Ecstasy, the real sublime experience, as a mystic might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means heavenly or delicate, close in sense to sublime.

clue.text: English article can split page, foreign article being the polished article?

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a tin is a can
a gap is a split or opening
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: An English piece splits a page while a foreign piece is presented as the finished product.
explanation.walkthrough: Dessert apples are often polished to a shine before eating.
explanation.definitionFit: An eating apple is one for eating raw, often rubbed shiny, so it is the polished article.

clue.text: Wow! Not entirely trim, but bit of a looker

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow

indicators.note: not entirely says the last letter of the word for trim is dropped

parts.note: neat means trim or tidy

explanation.surface: Someone admires a figure that is not quite trim but still attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the clear front part of the eye, a part of something that looks.

clue.text: Mysterious power slowing vivacity

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is a mysterious mental power
rit, short for ritardando, is the musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: Some uncanny force is draining someone's liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit means liveliness of mind or spirit, a synonym of vivacity.

clue.text: Cat gutted, which is rank

indicators.note: gutted means the middle is removed, so the central letter goes

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat has been disembowelled, which smells rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level in a series, a rank.

clue.text: See 7
Light fixture

definitions.meaning: a small stick struck to make a flame
a sporting contest arranged between two sides

explanation.definitionFit: A match is both a stick that lights and a scheduled game.

clue.text: Bird winding others up

indicators.note: winding with up suggests winding something back, so the word is turned around
in a down clue, up says the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: auks are other seabirds, so they stand for others here

explanation.surface: A bird teases its fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' stands for other birds, AUKS; reading it upwards gives the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a predatory seabird that chases other birds for their food.

clue.text: Champion losing lead becomes bit of a target

indicators.note: losing lead means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a winner is a champion

explanation.surface: A champion falls from the top and becomes a mere part of the target.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner is the ring of a target just outside the bull.

clue.text: In duel, 'e's taken out fat bore

indicators.note: taken out says a letter is removed from the word for a fight

parts.note: the letter E, written as a dropped-aitch word
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: In a duel, someone is taken out by a fat, boring opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: ''e's taken out' sounds like 'he is killed'; it means the letter E is removed from DUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow, boring person, a bore.

clue.text: Terribly dry in county shortly requiring water source

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another
shortly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of dry are scrambled

explanation.surface: A county in a terrible drought needs a source of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the usual short form of Hampshire, a county in southern England; 'shortly' trims it further, and 'Terribly' scrambles the dry letters to YDR before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrant is a street outlet supplying water, as for fire hoses.
